paper_id: Exploring Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Model on Automated Program Repair
title: Exploring Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Model on Automated Program Repair
motivation: FMFT demands significant computing resources which may be not practical for all users; limited research on PEFT for APR
problem_framing: Investigate PEFT effectiveness/efficiency on APR with execution-based evaluation; construct APR-specific instruction dataset
key_insight: IA3 outperforms other PEFT methods by improving LLM creativity rather than just pattern similarity matching
method_signature: PEFT (LoRA/prefix-tuning/p-tuning v2/IA3) fine-tuning LLMs on APR-Instruction with test-based patch validation
evaluation_criteria: pass@k metrics on Defects4J/QuixBugs/HumanEval-Java; peak GPU memory and trainable parameter counts
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: FMFT performed inferior to both no fine-tuning and PEFT methods due to overfitting with limited dataset
evidence_for_taste: FMFT performed inferior to both no fine-tuning
does not ensure that executing the two code segments will produce similar
high-quality patches ranked within the top 10
Improving the rank blindly does not necessarily yield further improvements
larger parameter size in FMFT may increase the risk of overfitting
thinking_moves: 把APR的评估标准从语法相似度转向功能正确性验证
发现FMFT在有限数据上过拟合的问题,转而强调PEFT的效率优势
通过creativity分析解释IA3优于其他PEFT方法的原因
发现参数规模与训练数据大小与PEFT效果不成正比
